name: Kingdom of Great Britain (George II)

areaKm2.note: world_1715 United Kingdom (Great Britain) 205,174 km2 + Kingdom of Ireland 82,955 km2 on the sphere = 288,129 km2; Great Britain is ~229,000 km2 in reality, so high allows for the coarse coastline.

population.note: HYDE via OWID: United Kingdom (modern borders, incl. Northern Ireland) 9,288,177 (1750) and 9,823,145 (1760); plus the rest of Ireland. Wrigley-Schofield England 1756 ~6.1M, Webster's Scotland 1755 1.27M, Ireland ~2.4M -> ~10M for the British crowns incl. Ireland. Colonies excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: United Kingdom 23.2% (1750); de Vries gives England 16.7% (towns 10,000+, 1750); Ireland and Scotland lower. Mid 20%.

activePersonnel.note: Brewer, The Sinews of Power (1989) table 2.1: Seven Years War annual average ~93,000 army (British and Irish establishments incl. colonies, excluding Hanoverian and Hessian troops in British pay) and ~74,000-82,000 navy; the Dutch States Navy table gives British naval personnel 85,000 in 1760 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_States_Navy). 1759 near the peak.

trainedReserves.note: Embodied county militia under the Militia Act 1757: ~17,000 in 1759 rising to ~30,000 (Brewer ch. 2); counted as trainedReserves per convention. German auxiliaries in British pay (~50,000) excluded.

supportPersonnel.note: Navy and marines ~80,000-85,000 (85,000 personnel in 1760, Dutch States Navy table after Rodger and Glete), Royal Artillery (~2,500, 30+ companies), engineers and the Board of Ordnance staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak forces ~200,000 incl. militia (Brewer table 2.1) on ~10M = 2%; ceiling 4-5% (reached in the Napoleonic Wars with volunteers).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Marching regiments of foot (~70 numbered regiments in 1759 at ~800-1,000) and Foot Guards, at home, in Germany (Minden 1759), North America (Quebec 1759), the West Indies and India (Brewer table 2.1 total less cavalry and artillery).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: Brown Bess flintlock and bayonet, platoon firing

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service professionals; Minden (1 Aug 1759) and Quebec (13 Sept 1759) volleys

count.note: Educated guess: light infantry companies, Rogers' Rangers, the 80th Light Armed Foot (Gage's) in North America.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: rifled carbines for some

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: trained for forest warfare

count.note: Household Cavalry, regiments of Horse and Dragoon Guards.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: big horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional; mishandled at Minden (Sackville)

count.note: Dragoon and the new light dragoon regiments (from 1759; e.g. Eliott's 15th). Dragoons counted as light cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: light dragoons new

count.note: Educated guess: field pieces of the Royal Artillery across all theatres (Germany, America, India), excl. fortress and naval guns.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Board of Ordnance standard guns, Woolwich

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Royal Military Academy Woolwich (1741)

count.note: Rodger, The Command of the Ocean (2004) appendix of fleet strength: Royal Navy ships of the line in sea pay ~100-120 in 1759-60; Hawke had 24 at Quiberon Bay (20 Nov 1759, Battle of Quiberon Bay article after Bodart). The Dutch States Navy table counts 230 British warships of all classes in 1760.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 74-gun ships entering service (copied from captured French designs); robust three-deckers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Western Squadron close blockade, Lagos and Quiberon Bay 1759: the best seamanship and gunnery of the era

count.note: Frigates, sloops, bomb vessels and fireships: 230 warships in 1760 (Dutch States Navy table) less ~110 ships of the line.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: new 32- and 36-gun frigates

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: constant sea time

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Pitt's global strategy; Hawke, Boscawen at sea; Wolfe (Quebec), Ferdinand of Brunswick (Minden, allied command); Cabinet and Admiralty coordination

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: regimental identity, long service; navy crews pressed but cohesive

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Annus Mirabilis 1759: Minden, Lagos, Quebec, Quiberon Bay, Guadeloupe

weapons.note: Anchor: 5.85 near 6 (1805). Evidence: Brown Bess flintlock, light 6-pdrs

armor.note: Anchor: 5.7. Evidence: no body armour except heavy cavalry breastplates (largely abandoned)

ships.note: Anchor: 5.9 near 6 (74-gun ships of the line). Evidence: the first British 74s and copper experiments (1761)

fortification.note: Anchor: 5.7. Evidence: Vauban-type defences at Portsmouth, Plymouth, Gibraltar

logistics.note: Anchor: 5.7. Evidence: Victualling Board, the best naval supply system of the era; transport fleets across the Atlantic

communications.note: Anchor: 5.6. Evidence: Admiralty courier and packet-boat network

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): United Kingdom 1756 = 2,643, 1759 = 2,850 (Great Britain series). Ireland poorer (~1,300-1,600); mid 2,550 is the weighted value incl. Ireland.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Brewer ch. 2: military spending ~70% of government expenditure in the Seven Years War, government spending ~15-20% of national income in war years; peacetime (1750s) ~4%. Wartime mid ~10%.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Crafts/Harley-type shares put industry at ~25-30% of English output c. 1760; Ireland and Scotland lower.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: England was a grain exporter until the 1760s; high agricultural productivity.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: turnpike trusts covered ~15,000 miles (~24,000 km) by 1770; Wade's military roads in Scotland ~400 km.

majorPorts.note: Portsmouth, Plymouth, Chatham, Sheerness, Deptford/Woolwich, London, Bristol, Liverpool, Glasgow, Cork, Dublin, Leith, Harwich, Falmouth.

merchantTonnage.note: English merchant shipping ~420,000 tons (1751) to ~520,000 tons (1763) burden in Ralph Davis's series (The Rise of the English Shipping Industry), plus Scottish and colonial-registered shipping; tons burden converted roughly to deadweight. Grade C.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Overseas, sea transport supplied expeditions across the Atlantic and to India.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses (~1M in England and Wales) plus Irish and Scottish stock and oxen.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: sea moat and Royal Navy, loyal population, fortified dockyards; the 1759 French invasion plan failed at sea.

notes: Snapshot = 1759, the Annus Mirabilis of the Seven Years War. Population: Great Britain and Ireland (the Irish establishment of the army is counted); American colonies, India presidencies and West Indies are bases only, and colonial provincial troops and East India Company sepoys are excluded. Personnel convention: regular army and navy are active; embodied militia is trainedReserves; Hanoverian, Hessian and Brunswick troops in British pay are excluded. Ship-of-the-line count depends on whether ships in ordinary are included (the mid counts ships in sea pay).
